FADE IN:
A PLAY-DOH MAN walks into FRAME.
It was like any day in Play-Doh Village...
BOOM. BOOM. BOOM. The street begins to SHAKE. The Play-Doh
man reacts to the strangeness -- what could it be? RUNS FOR THE
HILLS. A GIANT REPTILIAN FOOT STOMPS INTO FRAME.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...except today was the day death came.
It’s YOUNG NED and YOUNG CHUCK in their RODAN and GODZILLA
costumes, respectively. They stomp through the village.
The Play-Doh man shoves an OLD WOMAN out of the way and is
STOMPED. PLAY-DOH MAN #2 runs past, attempting to escape. But
Young Ned reaches down and picks him up and PUNTS HIM.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Young Ned enjoyed bringing Play-Doh death to
Play-Doh people. He did not yet realize he
could bring real death to real people.
Play-Doh Man #2 flies INTO FRAME and IRISES US TO:

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG CHUCK’S HOUSE - FLASHBACK (PILOT RE-USE)

lines.text: Young Chuck, in full-on Godzilla gear, rushes around the yard as
her FATHER hoses her off.
Young Chuck was 8 years, 42 weeks, 3 hours and 2
minutes old... and about to become an orphan.
Chuck GIGGLES with delight, running in circles through the
spray, amidst the Play-Doh carnage. Chuck, soaked, heads up the
front stairs of her porch, through the door and into her house.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Her father washed off the grit from a hard day
conquering villages...
Chuck’s father goes back to watering the lawn.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...then turned his attention to an irksome dry
patch in the lawn. Irksome because no amount
of watering or fertilizer or...
Chuck’s father drops dead in the grass.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...then the dry patch didn’t matter anymore.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. YOUNG CHUCK’S HOUSE - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Ned sits opposite NED’S MOTHER, who has her arm around Chuck.
Both Chuck and Ned are in states of shock. Chuck holds a pocket
watch in her hand.
CLOSE ON THE POCKET WATCH
Chuck rubs her tiny thumb over the CC engraving.
Chuck’s father wasn’t just a star in her life,
he was a pocket universe full of stars.
ON NED AND NED’S MOTHER
She forces a smile while he can’t be bothered to pretend he’s
anything but shell-shocked.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Ned and his mother waited with Chuck for her
aunts Lily and Vivian to arrive. Chuck would
later remember Ned being very quiet, staring
at his mother as if staring at a ghost.
Ned stares at his mother, horrified.
Only Ned knew his mother had already been dead
once that day.
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Young Ned’s mother, shaking her head:
NED’S MOTHER
There but for the grace of God.
Only Ned knew that he had touched her back to
life and one minute later, Chuck’s father died.
Young Ned is deliberately avoiding eye contact with Chuck.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It had seemed to Ned a strange coincidence. A
strange, troubling coincidence. Chuck would
remember Ned didn’t look at her.
LILY and VIVIAN, dressed in black from head to toe, drag steamer
trunks on wheels into the house. Ned and Ned’s mother stand.
Vivian immediately embraces Chuck, who seems too tired to cry.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
She would remember Vivian, who didn’t like to
touch anyone, was the first to embrace her.
Lily stands back, as if behind a force field, staring at Chuck.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And she would remember Lily, who had no
problem with touch at all, couldn’t bring
herself within reach... not right away.

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG CHUCK’S HOUSE - PORCH - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Young Ned rings the doorbell, still wearing his pajamas. The
door opens to REVEAL Lily. Lily looks down at Young Ned, who is
still in shock after witnessing his mother’s death. She reacts
and quickly pulls him into a hug. Vivian and Young Chuck come
down the stairs, wondering what the commotion is about.
Chuck would remember Ned ringing the doorbell
just after bedtime. And Lily telling her:
Something happened.
(gasps)
Another something happened?
Lily releases Ned from the hug and turns and holds Chuck,
catching the young girl by surprise.
It wasn’t until Lily hugged Young Ned after
learning of his mother’s second and final
passing, that she took Chuck in her arms.
As Lily continues to hold onto Chuck for dear life, Vivian
gently pulls Ned inside.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And when she did... she wouldn’t let go.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG CHUCK’S HOUSE - STREET - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Chuck steps outside just in time to hear the RUMBLE of a car
engine. NED’S FATHER’S PLYMOUTH pulls out of the driveway.
It was no less difficult for Chuck to let go
of Ned when his father whisked him away to be
abandoned at the Longborough School for Boys.
POV THROUGH BACK WINDOW: Chuck runs after the car. Ned stares
out the side window, so despondent he doesn’t notice Chuck.
Ned! Ned!
Chuck’s figure vanishes into the horizon as the car pulls away.
Chuck would never see him again... not for as
long as she lived.
ON CHUCK
She stands in the middle of the road.
ADULT NED (O.S.)
Chuck?!
Young Chuck turns to see who called her name.
OMIT
TIME CUT TO:
CLOSE ON A SNOWFLAKE
It falls TOWARD AND PAST CAMERA...
It’s 20 years, 2 months, 3 weeks, 2 days, 5
hours and 54 minutes later... but this winter...
ADULT NED (O.S.)
Chuck?!
SNOW FALLS, blanketing the city in a sheen of white. THE CAMERA
DRIFTS through the street until:
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
...there’s an unpleasant chill in the air.
After learning her father died because the Pie-
Maker brought his mother back to life...
CAMERA FINDS NED, clad only in his pajamas, a robe and some
winter boots, shivering in the cold. (NOTE: He should be
wearing his pj’s from the last scene of “Bitter Sweets.”)
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Chuck disappeared into the night.
A few flecks of snow melt on his cheeks, like tears.
(calling out)
Chuck?!
No response. He continues to shuffle through the snow.
NED (CONT’D)
Chuck?!
ANGLE - A WINDOW
A window SLAMS OPEN and a burly ANGRY NEIGHBOR shouts:
Stop squawking for your boyfriend, you twit--
Before the burly angry neighbor can finish, WHACK -- he’s hit in
the face with a snowball.
ON NED
Ned is already packing another snowball. He swings back and
throws. WHACK. It hits the side of the window and explodes
into dust. The angry neighbor backs down and shuts his window.
Ned goes back to stomping through the street, calling for:
Chuck?!
The Pie-Maker considered the places to find
Chuck... the places she’d roam...
Ned stands on the front porch and knocks on the door. Drifts of
snow have collected on most surfaces.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
...the places she called home.
Finally, a shotgun barrel slides through the mail slot and
levels itself at Ned’s knee. Then:
VIVIAN (O.S.)
(clears her throat)
Who is it?
It’s um... Ned... the pie-maker.

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

lines.text: Both Lily and Vivian are bundled in layers of winter coats.
And all this fuss about global warming...
Can’t happen soon enough, if you ask me.
Why is it so cold in here?
Charlotte used to light the furnace. The
thought of outliving her seemed so unlikely we
never bothered to learn how to do it.
So it hasn’t mysteriously lit itself recently,
because clearly it’s very cold.
Clearly.
Wouldn’t it be lovely if Charlotte’s ghost
returned to light the furnace?
Would you like me to light the furnace?
TIME CUT TO:
MINUTES LATER
Ned is slightly dirty from lighting the furnace and Lily and
Vivian have taken off all their coats. Much better.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
On the subject of Charlotte’s ghost... if you
sense her presence in any way--
When you say “presence”...?
If you think you see her out of the corner of
your eye or hear strange noises in her room or
find suspicious footprints in the snow...
Should we be expecting this presence ‘cause
you’re being kind of urgent over there?
Oh god, no. I’m just, uh, thawing. But if
you were to see her or think you see her--
I saw Charlotte once. After she died. Then I
blinked and she was gone. It was unpleasant.
That trick my mind played on me. And it’s
unpleasant for you to come here picking scabs
in the middle of the night.
I didn’t mean to pick.
Lily and Vivian both stand.
Thank you very much for lighting our furnace
so Charlotte’s ghost wouldn’t have to.
Am I leaving?
CUT TO:
Ned stands on the stoop as the door SLAMS shut behind him.

scenes.heading: INT. NED’S APARTMENT BUILDING - HALLWAY - MORNING

lines.text: Ned knocks on Olive’s door. The door swings open to REVEAL
OLIVE, in pj’s, brushing her teeth.
Hiya. Did you come to get Digby?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
She spits toothpaste foam into a cup and wipes her mouth.
No. Have you seen Chuck?
Not since your chorus of slamming doors last
night that woke me from a dead sleep.
Oh. Did we get loud?
You got very loud. After all the commotion, I
peeped my peeper out the peephole, saw her
getting in the elevator and you taking the
stairs. Take it you didn’t catch her.
That elevator’s fast and the stairs were slippery.
I heard you walking the streets moaning her name
like someone out of a Tennessee Williams. It
may be romantic, but it’s not dignified.
I don’t know where she is, Olive.
Maybe she don’t want you to know. Now go
clean yourself up, you look like hell.
With that, Olive slowly shuts the door, keeping an eye on Ned’s
reaction until she’s gone.
It was hard for Olive Snook to close the door
on the Pie-Maker’s breaking heart.
OFF Ned, unsettled.
OMIT
Olive enters to find CHUCK sitting on her bed, petting DIGBY.
Are you gonna tell me what he did?
Chuck only shakes her head.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED:
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Did he beat you?
No.
Did he look like he wanted to beat you?
Olive.
A moment, then:
Is it over? You and... him.
No. I don’t know. I’m still digesting.
Well, I guess you can stay here until you’ve
passed whatever it is you’re digesting.
Thank you. Please don’t tell him where I am.
(then)
Did you shave Digby’s bum?
Chuck has noticed that there’s a bald patch on Digby’s bum.
No. Maybe he got it caught in the vacuum.
(to Digby)
That vacuum cleaner take a bite out of you?
Digby stares and puts his head down. Olive sits down next to
Chuck, moving in for the dirt.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
I know it’s none of my business, but I have so
many question tugging at my tongue as to why
you faked your death. I just felt like I had
to respect your privacy on that issue.
I appreciate that.
But I’m not gonna respect your privacy right
now. Why did you fake your death? Is this an
insurance scam? You and the pie-maker in some
kind of cahoots together?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (2)
We’re in cahoots. But not how you think.
(a long beat, then)
I died and he brought me back to life.
Cahoots enough for you?
If you don’t wanna tell me, then say so. I
was just curious if you’re fighting over the
cahoots or something more... personal.
More personal. And cahoots-related. Can we
go back to respecting my privacy?
Sure. Going to your aunts’ later, since
you’re avoiding Ned I guess you won’t be
making them a pie. Want me to grab one off
the rack?
Would you mind terribly making one for them?
From scratch? They like them a certain way.
Well, whatever way you been making ‘em is
doing the trick. The mermaids are swimming.
They’re back in the water?
Vivian told me. Lily didn’t want me to know.
Thought I’d gloat. So I’m pretending not to.
I’m pretending not to know a lot these days.
(then)
Pear with Gruyère baked into the crust?
Yes, please. And I add extra vanilla. It’s
my secret ingredient. Lily loves vanilla.
Chuck produces a dropper bottle of homeopathic antidepressants.
But Chuck’s secret ingredient wasn’t vanilla.
Olive uncaps the top of a dropper bottle and DRIP-DRIP-DRIPS it
onto the pie. She starts to put the top crust over the filling.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
It was an herbal mood enhancer. Olive Snook
had been delivering enhanced pies for weeks,
not realizing she was a homeopathic drug mule.
Olive tastes the vanilla, curious.
Not very strong vanilla.
She considers, then pours a whole lot more on the filling before
covering it with the top crust. Olive grates some cheese on the
crust and slides the pie into the oven and shuts the oven doors.
DINING AREA - ON NED AND EMERSON
They sit across from each other in a booth.
I told her I killed her father.
She ask you if you killed her father? She ask
you that? Those words came outta her mouth?
No. We were talking about phantom limbs, then
I blurted it out. It was like word vomit.
Then you slipped in that word vomit and fell
on your ass and now you covered in word vomit.
Dead Girl could be out there all grudgey-
grudge with a beef to pick. “Hello, Evening
News, I’m ‘Lonely Tourist’ Charlotte Charles.
I crawled outta my grave and here’s how.”
Stop it. I’m having difficulty breathing.
What kind of state she in?
A bad state. She just up and left. Now she’s
out there all alone in the cold, cold world.
Sound like she wants to be out there alone in
the cold, cold world. Don’t go tracking her
down and reminding her why she’s mad at you.
Then she will go to the Evening News.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED:
As Olive approaches:
That’s what I said. Except the “Evening News”
part, which I don’t understand.
(then)
We’re talking about Chuck, aren’t we?
We’re talking about Chuck. Him and me. I
don’t know what you’re talking about because
this chitchat doesn’t concern you. Shoo.
They stare at Olive until she gets the hint and moves off.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Dead Girl needs to sort out what she has to
sort out. You can’t go droppin’ a “I killed
your dad” bomb and expect happy-go-lightly. I
have a “Here’s what you should do:” Leave her
be. And while you’re leaving her be there’s
somebody I’d like you to talk to.
The facts were these...

scenes.heading: INT. ÜBER-LIFE LIFE INSURANCE - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: CAMERA PUSHES IN ON VICTOR NARRAMORE standing in front of the
Über-Life Life Insurance logo.
One Victor Narramore, an adjuster for Über-
Life Life Insurance, was 46 years, 11 weeks, 5
days, 17 hours and 3 minutes old...
CAMERA COMES OVER THE TOP OF A SNOWPLOW TO REVEAL: Victor’s
CORPSE is wedged in a pile of snow in front of it.
...when his body, frozen near solid, was
scooped up by a snowplow on the 200 block of
Oak Street. Unsettled by this particular New
Year’s tiding...
The PLOW DRIVER approaches Victor’s frozen body and hesitantly
pokes it a few times in confusion.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Oak Street Homeowner’s Association offered
a reward to find Victor Narramore’s killer.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 13.
The CORONER sits behind his desk wearing the ugliest Christmas
sweater ever, like ever. Ned and Emerson stand across from him.
People ask you why you wear that sweater?
My niece gave me this sweater for Christmas.
Thing’s uglier than a chipmunk’s ass.
He means the sweater, not your niece.
Why give a person a Christmas sweater for
Christmas? You can only wear it that day.
He means “should” only wear it that day.
Yeah. You either take off what you’re wearing
and put it on right then and there or you wait
a year for the next holiday season.
Why you going toe-to-toe with me on fashion?
Only thing I wanna hear out of you people is,
“Happy New Year.” And, “Here’s your rent.”
The coroner holds up his palm, waiting for it to be greased.
Happy New Year.
Here’s your rent.
Emerson greases it with a wad of cash. The coroner eyes him.
Feels light.
You’re just stronger than you think.
Mmm-hmm.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 14.
The FROZEN BODY OF VICTOR NARRAMORE slides out of the morgue
drawer, still frozen in the shape he was found in the snowbank.
Ned and Emerson exchange a look. Ned touches Victor’s frozen
body and we see him FLASH with life. But his eyes don’t open.
Finally, they pop open with a CRACKLE of ice.
Only Victor’s mouth and eyes move, everything else is frozen.
I can’t move.
You’re frozen solid.
So there is such a thing as a snowball’s
chance in hell? Or is this where the walls
burst into flame and you rip off your flesh
and reveal yourselves to be demons?
You’re not in hell, Mr. Narramore.
(then)
Should you be?
No, no. Of course not. Well... it really
depends on who you talk to.
(then)
Who am I talking to?
Angels of Justice.
Oh. Then I am in hell, aren’t I?
Who killed you, Mr. Narramore?
I don’t know who killed me. But I do know how
they killed me.
Victor Narramore walks to HIS CAR with a group of other MEN and
WOMEN (Note: To include KEVIN VANDEN EYKEL and BILL RICHTER).
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 15.
CONTINUED:
Victor waves goodbye to the group, then stops at his car as the
others continue walking. CAMERA FOLLOWS HIM ON HIS BACK as he
lifts up his key and clicks: BEEP-BEEP.
After a long day at the office, Victor
Narramore was walking to his car when he heard
someone approaching rapidly from behind.
We HEAR the rush of footsteps running up behind Victor. He
turns quickly, in time to see:
VICTOR’S POV - SLOW MOTION
A BASEBALL BAT with the word “KINDNESS” carved into it comes
into FOCUS as it’s being swung toward Victor’s head.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Victor Narramore didn’t see who killed him,
but he did see how he was killed. And he was,
in fact, killed with Kindness.
Right before impact, we CUT BACK TO:
As before.
You were killed with kindness?
Not the sentiment, which would have been
lovely, but the word, which was scratched into
the business end of a baseball bat.
Somewhere between Kindness and the morgue,
someone made you a corpsicle and you got
scooped up by a snowplow.
(feigning innocence)
I wonder why.
Really? You got to wonder? No idea why
someone would wanna kill you?
Well... I am an insurance adjuster. We’re
more hated than parking enforcement.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 16.
CONTINUED:
How come?
It’s my job to quantify people’s lives and
decide if they deserve a new organ that’ll allow
them to live. Most people don’t deserve a new
organ, that tends to be upsetting. No one wants
to be told if they should live or die.
(then)
Do I get to live now?
Ned checks his watch:
No.
Ned touches Victor Narramore and he FLASHES dead, but remains in
his near-frozen state like a citizen of Pompeii.
Need to get a list of folks who wanted a new
organ and were rejected by Victor Narramore.
But the Pie-Maker didn’t care about Victor
Narramore and his unattainable organs...
Emerson eyes a very distracted Ned.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He only cared about his attainable-yet-
unattainable Chuck...

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - ROOFTOP - DAY

lines.text: The roof is blanketed with snow.
...out there alone in the cold, cold world.
CAMERA FINDS Chuck looking out over the city, at a loss. Her
beehives are all covered to protect them from the cold.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But what he didn’t know...
MYSTERIOUS POV
As it approaches Chuck from behind.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...was that she wasn’t alone at all.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 17.
CONTINUED:
She HEARS a creak from the stairs behind her. She turns,
assuming it could only be:
Ned?
After a moment, OSCAR VIBENIUS steps onto the rooftop.
Not Ned.
OFF THAT...
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - ROOFTOP - DAY

lines.text: As before. Chuck and Oscar face off.
In winter everything’s dampened and hushed...
sounds and smells... but not you. The girl
who smells like honey and something like death
but not death. Something else altogether.
Hello, Oscar.
I hope your bees are surviving the chill.
Seem to be.
That explains the honey. But not the
something like death but not death.
It’s cold. I’m going in.
He offers a familiar sweater (as seen in “Smell of Success”),
holding it so she can put her arms through the sleeves.
This will keep you warm.
That’s my sweater.
She stares at it.
It’s clean, if that’s what you’re worrying
about. In fact, it’s very clean. I collected
every last bit of anything that wasn’t
cashmere. Even a small sample of your hair.
This is all making me very uncomfortable.
You mean up on a rooftop with a near stranger
who’s waxing on about collecting your hair?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED:
Yes. Wait. Did you shave Digby’s bum?
What is with you and that dog? You both have
that scent about you.
You did shave Digby’s bum.
I suppose I should have asked first. Which
reminds me: Could I bother you for a larger
sample of your hair? I only got a few strands
from the sweater. Can’t do much with that.
What’re you gonna do with it?
Stuff it in my pillow. Human hair is so much
softer than down. I’m teasing you. I’m just
curious why you and the dog aren’t like
everyone else. Hair can be very telling about
so many things. Unless you already know what
the hair knows and care to tell me yourself.
The hair doesn’t know anything. Maybe it’s
you. People experience strange smells that
aren’t actually there all the time.
People with neurological disorders. Are you
suggesting I have a neurological disorder
that’s affecting my olfactory glands?
You do spend a lot of time in the sewer.
Some of us belong underground. Sewer life has
only honed my sense of smell. If you were in
a white room, you’d only see white. But white
is the presence of all color and that’s what I
see in the sewer. Or in this case, smell.
You can’t have any of my hair.
Then the dog’s ass shavings will have to do.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED: (2)
He turns to leave, but stops at the covered beehives.
OSCAR (CONT’D)
Bees. The Ancient Egyptians believed they
were inexorably entwined with death. They
used honey to mummify their dead and left jars
of it in the tombs for food in the afterlife.
You know a lot about bees.
And I suspect you know a lot about death.
(then)
If you change your mind about the hair, I’m
just a flush away.
And with that, he’s gone...
Exhausted, Ned stands in the kitchen looking out to the front
windows, waiting for Chuck to return. The back door opens and
Olive enters...
Boy, it’s cold. You could use a witch’s bosom
as a hot-water bottle on a day like today.
Any sign of Chuck?
Olive gets to work around the room, enjoying the conversation
with herself:
“And how are you, Olive?” I’m fine, thanks for
asking, Ned. “That was a funny joke about the
witch’s bosom, Olive.” Thank you, Ned. “And I
appreciate you saying ‘bosom.’” Why, because
it is less offensive than other words, Ned?
“No, because I simply like the word ‘bosom,’
Olive. I say it to myself all the time.
Bosom. Bosom. Bosom. I can’t help myself. I
am a bosomahaulic.”
A moment, then:
Are you done?
Think so.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
You promise me you don’t know where she is?
How would I know where she is?
Because I keep going over this in my mind and
Chuck doesn’t know many people and you’re not
one of the many people she doesn’t know.
Have you slept at all?
Did you know you have a tell when you lie?
Do I?
You answer questions with questions.
Maybe I know I have a tell and I know you know
I have a tell and I’m doing it now to confuse
you so you don’t know what tell I’m telling.
But why would you go to the trouble of answering
questions with questions and pretending to lie
if you really don’t know where she is?
Can you tell me?
The bells on the door RING, rescuing Olive. Ned looks out
hopefully, then sees it’s Emerson.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - CONTINUOUS

lines.text: As Ned joins Emerson in his booth.
Victor Narramore turned down fifteen folks for
organ transplants and out of those fifteen
folks, three are viable persons of interest.
Why are only three viable?
Because twelve are not viable.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 22.
CONTINUED:
Oh.
(getting it)
Oh.
One of those viable persons of interest lives
on the two hundred block of Oak Street. Abner
Newsome. Got turned down last year for a new
heart. By Victor Narramore.
(nods)
You getting on the trolley?
Is Abner Newsome still alive?
Hence viable.
I should wait here for Chuck. Just in case.
You just don’t wanna talk to a sick child. I
understand. It’s a hard, sad life.
Are you really trying to make me feel guilty
when I am this depressed?
I’m trying to get you out of your depression.
You don’t need me to talk to the living.
Suit yourself. But Dead Girl don’t need you
either. You the last person she needs to see
right now which is why she ain’t here.
Emerson scoots out of the booth, leaving Ned to gaze absently
out the window. CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Olive, who has clocked this
last exchange from afar...
OMIT
Chuck is looking out the window as Olive pulls on her coat and
grabs Digby’s leash and places it around his collar. She picks
up a pie box, getting ready to head out.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 23.
CONTINUED:
Before I head out I want you to take a mental
picture of me, your friend Olive, here with
Digby on my way to deliver your aunts a
delicious pie, which I do as your friend.
Thank you.
Did you take your picture?
Yes.
Olive unlocks the front door. Ned is standing there.
Look. It’s Ned.
Chuck sees him. Olive grabs her coat and a big fur hat and
heads out with Digby on his leash, hiding the pie box from Ned.
Did you shave Digby’s--
We don’t know how that happened.
(then)
Okay. See ya.
Olive exits, shuts the door. Ned stares at Chuck, but she
averts her eyes.
Been looking.
Been hiding.
How much does Olive know?
Don’t worry about Olive. Even if I did tell
her I died and you brought me back to life,
she wouldn’t believe me.
You don’t know that.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 24.
CONTINUED: (2)
Yes, I do. Because I told her and she didn’t
believe me.
Why would you do that?
Because I needed to tell somebody the truth.
Even if they didn’t believe me. I just wanted
to tell the truth about who I am. And what
happened to me and what you did to my dad.
Can’t we keep the truth between you and me?
It’s hard to keep the truth between you and me
when it’s so hard to look at you now.
Ned’s heart is breaking.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
I remember when you came over that night after
my dad died. You wouldn’t look at me either.
If I looked at you, I felt... too much.
You knew you killed him. That’s why you
couldn’t look at me and that’s why I can’t
look at you now.
Ned nods, trying to keep his emotion in check.
Chuck... please.
No one could tell me how my dad died. I
thought it was the fickle finger of fate. But
it wasn’t the fickle finger of fate. It was
your fickle finger. That one, right there.
I didn’t mean my finger to be fickle. I
didn’t know what it would do.
I know. I rationalized the whole thing. It
was like you were playing with a gun and it
accidentally went off and killed my dad.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 25.
CONTINUED: (3)
Like that. Except there’s no gun and I wasn’t
playing. My mother died. But yeah, I’m the
kid who killed your dad. And I hate that.
I hate that, too.
Do you hate... me?
She’s silent for a long beat, then:
I have to hate you a little for just a little
while... and I can’t hate you if you’re here.
I don’t want you to hate me. I should stay.
If you stay I’ll just end up hating you more.
(then)
Just go.
Ned stares at her, dumbfounded. Then walks out the door. After
a beat, Chuck sighs, exhausted from the whole exchange.
Chuck considered how much easier circumstances
would be if she had someone to talk to who
wasn’t the Pie-Maker... someone who might
believe her secrets if she told them...
CLOSE ON - A NOTE
It reads: “Meet me on the roof.” REVEAL WE ARE--
Chuck stands over the toilet. She wads up the note and throws
it in the bowl, flushing.
...someone else who belonged underground.
Emerson walks from HIS CAR up the path to a modest suburban
home, past a big snowman on the snow-covered lawn.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 26.
CONTINUED:
Hot on the trail of an ice-cold killer, Mr.
Cod paid a visit to the third of his 3 persons
of interest in the murder of Über-Life Life
Insurance adjuster Victor Narramore.

scenes.heading: INT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - DAY

lines.text: Emerson sits at a kitchen table across from ABNER NEWSOME (14),
a scowling, wheelchair-bound curmudgeon with a heart condition.
The facts were these...
CLOSE ON ABNER’S SCOWL.
A DOCTOR holds up a smiling, fresh-from-the-baby-maker BABY.
Abner Newsome was a happy child...
The doctors SLAPS the baby’s ass to start it breathing. It
opens its mouth and WAILS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...for the first 34 seconds of his life...
CLOSE IN on the darkness of its mouth. CUT TO:

scenes.heading: INT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM

lines.text: PULL BACK from the black glint of Abner’s scowl. We’re in Abner
Newsome’s living room that has been decorated with a ridiculous
amount of SPORTS MEMORABILIA and ARCADE-STYLE VIDEO GAMES. He
sits in his WHEELCHAIR.
...whereupon it was discovered that he suffered
from a debilitating heart condition... that left
him sad, sick and very, very surly.
EMMA NEWSOME peels potatoes into a bucket as she sits in an easy
chair next to her son’s HOSPITAL BED that’s set up in the living
room in front of a BIG-SCREEN TELEVISION that’s playing the 1938
Warner Brothers classic, “Adventures of Robin Hood.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As the single mother of a sickly, surly child --
Emma Newsome was a raw nerve her son would often
peel like a potato.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 27.
CONTINUED:
PULL BACK: As Emma viciously peels, Emerson crosses his legs.
When I saw you coming up the block I thought
you might be from the Wish-a-Wish Foundation.
Or another charity. Or a celebrity. Or a
celebrity representing a charity.
That’s nice. Must be nice for your son to
know there’s people that care.
Yeah, caring is great. Love the caring. Know
what would be even better? Not dying.
Abner, this is Emerson Cod. He’s investigating
a crime.
I heard on the news that that Narramore guy got
whacked. He turned me down for a good heart
once, so he can pretty much suck it, I think.
You don’t seem too... bereft at his passing.
I’m not. Not at all. In fact, when he’s done
sucking it he can eat my dump.
Abner.
(catching on)
Oh, please tell me I’m a suspect. Awesome.
‘Cause first I took a magic potion that made
the tissue-paper sack I call my heart work.
Then I stepped on his neck with the soggy,
atrophied breadsticks that used to be my legs.
My son is very sick, Mr. Cod.
I can see that.
If you’re not here to grant a wish or give us
free merchandise, then I think you should leave.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 28.
CONTINUED: (2)
Emerson stands.
Don’t let the door hit you on your big
oxygenated blood-filled ass on the way out.
You’re pushing it.
If I piss you off, are you gonna sneeze and
kill me?
Have a nice day.
If you have any more questions, I’ll be right
here. Or slumped in a pile on the floor.
Emerson exits--
The door SLAMS as Emerson walks back down the path, his angry
thoughts distracted by--
ANGLE - A SNOWMAN
A STRAY DOG is peeing on the snowman’s base...
(smiles)
Good dog. Good dog. Why don’t you leave a
little present there for ‘em, too.
(off the dog)
Don’t be lookin’ at me like I’m evil.
Something catches Emerson’s attention. He approaches the yellow
snow as the dog runs off. The yellow snow has melted away
REVEALING A FOOT. Emerson starts brushing the rest of the snow
off, REVEALING A LEG...
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Mmm-mmm.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 29.
FADE IN:
OMIT
Emerson and Ned stand in front of a gurney. A pair of ICY FEET
stick out from the bottom of the sheet covering the body.
Having followed the frozen stiff from Abner
Newsome’s house to the morgue, Emerson Cod
grew concerned...
I’m concerned.
About Chuck?
About you and your moonin’ over Dead Girl.
You gotta pull yourself together. We got a
corpsicle to question!
Reluctant, Ned pulls back the sheet revealing:
ANOTHER FROZEN MAN in his underwear, covered in a thin lair of
frost and ice.
Ned starts his watch and touches the corpse. Nothing happens.
He shoots Emerson a concerned look and tries again. Nothing.
Wha--?
Emerson sighs. Takes out his knitting needles. And chisels a
HOLE in the layer of ice revealing bare skin.
Freezer burn... try again.
Ned starts his watch and with the FAMILIAR POP OF ELECTRICITY,
our dead man, BILL, sits up, ice cracking around his limbs.
Bill Richter, Über-Life Life Insurance. If
you’ve got big problems, we’ve got bigger
solutions. That’s life. Über-Life.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 30.
CONTINUED:
Another Über-Life insurance agent.
Actually, I prefer “insurance adjuster.” It’s
my job to assess damage.
Maybe it’s time for a self-assessment.
Bill looks down at his frozen, beaten body.
(looks down)
Oh, this? Guess that’s what happens when
you’re smacked with a bat.
Any idea who smacked you?
No. But you might want to ask Kevin.
NED / EMERSON
Kevin?
Kevin Vanden Eykel. We carpool. We’d just
left the others and headed for my car where I
was fumbling for my keys, when all of a sudden
I hear him scream, “Watch out!”
(then)
Next thing you know, here I am.
(then)
Where am I?
You’re, um... in the morgue.
Oh. If I’m dead...
(clocks Ned’s sad expression)
...then why are you the one with the long face?
Ned is taken aback. Emerson is annoyed.
BILL RICHTER (CONT’D)
Lemme guess. Girl problems?
Hell no.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 31.
CONTINUED: (2)
Hell yes. I can see it in his eyes. What’s
her name?
Well, I call her Chuck, but that’s not her
real name. It’s sort of a funny story--
Ask the fool how he got in that snowman!
Snapping out of it, Ned turns to Emerson.
Sorry...
(sadly, to Bill)
I can’t talk about this right now.
Oh, that’s okay. It’ll come when you’re
ready. Till then...
Bill reaches sympathetically toward Ned and:
BILL RICHTER (CONT’D)
Chin up, big guy.
ZAP! Before Ned can react, Bill touches Ned’s chin and re-deads
in an instant. Emerson scowls.
I’m sorry. I thought I was pulled together...
then I... came apart.
Well you coming apart took apart our case. We
still don’t know a damn thing about this killer.
We don’t. But Kevin Vanden Eykel might...
OFF HIS LOOK...
OMIT
CLOSE ON: An “Über-Life Life Insurance” pamphlet with the
tagline “Debt or Death? Why Health Insurance Is a Good Bet.”
PULL BACK TO REVEAL Ned and Emerson are sitting across a desk
covered in mountainous stacks of client files.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 32.
CONTINUED:
An overworked, bespectacled pencil-pusher type enters. This is
STEVE KAISER.
You Kevin Vanden Eykel?
He drops another stack of files on his desk and takes a seat.
Nope, Steve Kaiser. I’ve been covering some
of Kevin’s cases since he went missing.
Emerson shoots Ned a look before turning back to Steve.
When’d he go missing?
Same night as Bill Richter and Victor Narramore.
(sadly)
In all probability, he’s dead like them.
‘Course the company won’t pay off on his policy
until the police find a body so his wife’s
struggling to keep her head above water. Now I
hear their youngest just broke his arm. When it
rains, it pours. I’m surprised they don’t just
cancel her insurance and put the final nail in
her coffin.
Doesn’t sound like you approve of how things
are done around here.
(suddenly paranoid)
Who’d you say you worked for again?
We didn’t... I’m a private investigator and
this is my associate.
Steve stands.
Then I think I’ve said enough. If you
gentlemen will excuse me--
Ned stands to block him.
Hold on. Bill Richter’s body ended up on the
front yard of a boy named Abner Newsome. All
we’re trying to do is find out why.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 33.
CONTINUED: (2)
From what we’ve gathered, Abner had applied to
Über-Life several times. Did Bill work on
Abner’s case?
Steve eyes them for a moment, then returns to his desk.
He types rapidly, then stares at the computer screen. Suddenly,
his face goes grim. He swings the screen around for them to see.
Bill, Victor and Kevin all rejected Abner for
a heart transplant.
That’s a little something we in the private
detective business like to call a pattern.
(nodding to Ned)
Let’s go...
Asses.
Excuse me?
Steve Kaiser appears agitated.
I’m talking about the suits who run this
company... Good god, how many people have to pay
the price before that boy finally gets a heart?
Then why don’t you just approve his application?
Because I’ll lose my job. Besides, it’s not up
to me. It’s up to the numbers. And his
number’s almost up. Low survival odds plus
exorbitant transplant costs equals bad business
and that’s the bottom line around here...
Hell, if this place has taught me anything,
it’s people are expendable.
OFF OF Emerson and Ned, we go...
OMIT

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - ROOFTOP - DAY

lines.text: Chuck looks out over the snow-covered city.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 34.
CONTINUED:
OSCAR (O.S.)
I got your invitation.
REVEAL Oscar has arrived behind her with the soaked note.
I’m glad you came. And scared. A little bit.
A small smile flashes across her lips...
Chuck felt alive holding the dark secret of
her death so close to the light of day.
The mystery of your scent is hardly solvable with
only the hair of a dog. But I have a hypothesis.
Hypothesize.
He moves closer. There’s a Hannibal/Clarice air to all this...
We are made up of our cells. The sum of our
parts. The cells I’ve smelled tell a story.
A cell starved for oxygen, as in death, will
reorganize its electrochemistry. Even after
life returns, the signature of the shock to
the system remains.
How?
There is always the slightest whiff of ozone,
like the fading memory of a dream.
Do I smell of ozone?
Your dog does. His hair contained one part
per million, but one part nonetheless. Did he
die and come back?
That would be impossible.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 35.
CONTINUED: (2)
People die and come back all the time. They
fall in frozen lakes, have heart attacks,
their lungs collapse. Then someone pulls them
back from the edge.
I would know if Digby fell into a frozen lake.
Perhaps you didn’t notice because you were
dying with him.
He watches her face a moment, then:
OSCAR (CONT’D)
It’s pure conjecture, of course. Based on
nothing but the hair of a dog’s behind...
Chuck could feel her truth stepping out of the
shadows, warming its toes in the sunshine.
And the man from the sewer could sense it...
It can be so exhausting to carry a secret.
I need a pair of scissors.
Oscar holds up a pair of scissors. She takes them, holds up a
section of her own hair and -- SNIP -- cuts it off...
CHUCK (CONT’D)
Tell me my secret.
She hands the hair to Oscar, who looks at her like he were
holding diamonds.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 36.
FADE IN:
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM

lines.text: Anticipating the arrival of a third body,
Emerson Cod and the Pie-Maker returned to the
house of the heartless boy...
Emma talks to Ned and Emerson by the doorway. Behind her:
Abner Newsome is sulking in his wheelchair at MADELINE McLEAN
(late 30s), a matronly headband-and-cardigans type woman with an
overeager smile to match her overly-sunny disposition.
Strangely enough, she’s holding a CUTE LITTLE MONKEY.
(ignoring the monkey)
Ma’am. The two insurance adjusters that died
were linked to Abner Newsome. We have reason
to believe a third one’s going to appear on
your lawn sometime soon.
That’s not good.
No -- it’s real good. ‘Cause this time, we’re
gonna be waitin’ outside to catch our iceman
when he cometh.
Suddenly, Madeline McLean approaches, still clutching her
monkey.
Thank goodness. A boy with a heart like
Abner’s doesn’t need any more stress.
Mr. Cod. This is Madeline McLean, she’s a
Wish-a-Wisher from the Wish-a-Wish Foundation.
And this is Bobo.
A bonobo?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 37.
CONTINUED:
(pleased)
I love a man who knows his monkeys. The
bonobo is the gentlest of primates. They’re
great with sick children. That’s why I’m
giving him to Abner.
Madeline holds up the monkey to Abner.
MADELINE MCLEAN (CONT’D)
Were you wishing for a cuddle?
Actually, I was wishing for a butter knife so I
could pop out its heart and use it as my own.
Okay then... No monkey.
(suddenly brightening)
I know -- how about tickets to Medieval Times?
On the list of things I’d like -- cuddling a
monkey and going to Medieval Times are right
next to constipation and diphtheria...
Madeline looks dejected. Ned and Emerson are uncomfortable.
But there must be some Wish-a-Wish wish you
wish for.
Suddenly, Abner looks tired. Defeated. You see him for the
sad, sickly, vulnerable boy he really is.
I wish you’d all just go away.
(swallows her disappointment)
Alrighty then.
I apologize for Abner. He’s been so sick lately.
I think he just needs some time alone...
Emma shows Emerson, Ned, Madeline and the monkey to the door.
We’ll be outside watching over you guys tonight.
As Emerson followed his instincts...
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 38.
Holding a pie box, Olive rings the doorbell, Digby at her side.
...Olive followed a familiar path to Chuck’s
aunts’ house.
CAMERA PUSHES INTO THE PIE BOX--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The Darling Mermaid Darlings overcame their
incapacitating social phobias with the help of
Chuck’s mood-enhancing pies.
CAMERA PULLS OUT OF THE PIE BOX...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But unbeknownst to all, this latest pie wasn’t
just dosed... it was over-dosed. It contained
a wallop of mood enhancers whose effects no
one could predict.
...REVEALING WE ARE NOW--

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM

lines.text: Olive stands in the middle of the room with Digby. Vivian sits
at a sewing machine, sewing MERMAID FINS. Lily stands nearby,
testing.
We’re making costumes for our next tour.
If we have a next tour. Is that pie? I have
been craving that pie all day.
The aunts had begun to hope again. Which left
Olive with one simple wish...
I sure wish Charlotte could see you like this.
Lily takes the pie box and opens it, pulling out a knife.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
None for me, thanks. I don’t like vanilla.
I’m in training.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 39.
CONTINUED:
I didn’t ask either of you if you wanted pie.
Maybe Charlotte can see us like this.
Evidently her ghost is about.
Really? Someone’s seen her ghost?
OMIT
Ned and Emerson on a stakeout. The wipers quietly SWISH, wiping
snow away from the windshield. Ned looks worried.
There’s a killer out there. Shouldn’t we be
doing something instead of just sitting here?
We’re not just sitting here. We’re following
a lead. Or in this case, a dead end. ‘Cause
we know that Kevin Vanden Eykel’s dead body’s
gonna end up here.
Shouldn’t we be investigating suspects?
Who? Only person with real motive right now
is Abner’s mom. But that’s just cold stupid.
Right. What kind of killer would leave her
victims on her own lawn?
We sit here long enough -- we’ll find out.
Ned begins fidgeting in his seat. Emerson’s annoyed.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Stop wiggle-worting. You’re steaming the
windows and giving the neighbors the wrong idea.
Sorry. I just hate sitting around and
waiting. But that’s all anyone seems to want
from me right now.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 40.
CONTINUED:
I know you’re not gonna start talkin’ ‘bout
Dead Girl at our stakeout.
I don’t want to. But I can’t help it. My
body’s staked-out here and my mind is staked-
out where she is. Wherever that is.
(then)
What do you think my chances are of getting
her back?
I look like a Ouija board to you?
What if Steve Kaiser was right and life works
like some big calculation where we take all
the good we’ve ever done and subtract the bad.
After what I’ve done--
(then)
What if Chuck and I don’t add up?
You add up.
(then)
To zero.
“Zero”? As in no hope?
Zero. As in zero dignity in dwelling on it.
And zero interest in discussing it.
You don’t understand.
Ned looks away, dejected. Emerson’s stung.
I understand more than you think. You feel
like you messed up. Lost the one person that
meant something to you. Part of you feels
like it’s for the best. Maybe you didn’t
deserve her anyway.
(haunted)
Still -- you want her back.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 41.
CONTINUED: (2)
(weirded out)
Okay. Maybe you do understand.
(then)
But there is something I can do to get Chuck
back. I could give her back her father. If
only to say goodbye.
You can’t go raisin’ Dead Girl’s dead dad.
It’ll give her peace of mind.
Oh, yeah? Well, I’m gonna give you a piece of
my mind. ‘Cause maybe you’re the one who
don’t understand this situation.
(then)
The relationship between a father and his
daughter... it’s tenuous. Fragile. It can
take a lifetime to work out all the issues
there. And you gonna try to “happily ever
after it” in a minute? You’re a dreamer.
And you’re a cynic.
(snaps)
I’m a father.
Ned’s mouth drops.
As in a priest?
As in a man with a daughter.
Ned’s mouth drops even wider.
You have a daughter? Where is she? Why don’t
you ever--
Uh-uh. Scratchin’ an itch just makes it
itchier. This is my itch and I sure as hell
don’t want you scratchin’ at it. Understood?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 42.
CONTINUED: (3)
(surrendering)
Understood. No scratching. My itches or yours.
The conversation over -- Emerson turns on the RADIO and stares
out the windshield.
Good. Now stay alert and look alive. We got
a killer to catch...
Emerson Cod focused back on the case...
OFF THE SADNESS IN HIS EYES...

scenes.heading: EXT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - STREET - NIGHT

lines.text: ...little knowing... someone else was focused
on Emerson and the Pie-Maker.
A PRESENCE creeps slowly toward the back of Ned’s car.
Emerson and Ned stare straight ahead -- focused on Abner
Newsome’s house. Unaware as:
The PRESENCE crouches below the car -- toward the tailpipe. We
see a gloved-hand reach out with a POTATO.
The hand PLUGS the tailpipe with the potato.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And their chances of staying alert... or
alive... were growing increasingly slim.
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 43.
FADE IN:
CLOSE ON Ned, as he opens his eyes from a very deep sleep.
Coughs. PULL OUT TO REVEAL the air in the car is smoky with
EXHAUST.
THROUGH THE DIVIDING GLASS
Emerson, also in a deep, poisoned sleep, the side of his face
SMOOSHED against the Plexi. Ned bangs on the glass.
Emerson! Wake up!
Emerson twitches, but does not wake. Ned opens his own door,
slides out onto the snowy ground, fighting grogginess, sucking
in air.
Ned stumbles around to the back of the car, leans down and PULLS
A POTATO out of the tailpipe. EXHAUST SPEWS OUT.
Ned stumbles around to the passenger side, opens the door and
pulls Emerson out onto the ground. Emerson takes a deep breath,
opens his eyes...
My head feels like it’s splitting in two.
It’s carbon monoxide poisoning. Someone put a
potato in our exhaust pipe.
Emerson looks at Ned, a thought occurring--
Tell me I’m not dead.
You’re not dead.
And I can be not-dead for more than a minute?
There are no minutes involved. You will
continue to be not-dead. Until you are dead.
But I have not undeaded you at any point.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 44.
CONTINUED:
Good.
You may be dying from breathing a poisonous
gas. But dead, no.
(notices)
Oh, hell...
Ned looks--
Realizing their lives were still lives...
ANGLE - ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE
Down the street, the POLICEMAN on patrol is also exiting his
smoke-filled car, coughing. On the pristine, snow-covered lawn
in front of Abner’s house stands ANOTHER SNOWMAN.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...the Pie-Maker and the Private Investigator
could not say the same for the body surely
frozen in the freshly-made snowman.
I used to love snowmen. Now I don’t.
A CRIME SCENE has been set up. Two POLICE CARS and the
CORONER’S VAN are all parked at the curb. The Newsome front
lawn has been crime-taped off. Ned and Emerson stand to the
side watching a plastic-gloved POLICE DETECTIVE yell at a sleepy-
looking policeman. The detective waves the snowman’s carrot
nose to make his point...
Watching the third insurance adjuster removed
from the front lawn of the Newsome house,
Emerson Cod, Private Investigator, drew an
intriguing conclusion:
We are giant, enormous idiots. And don’t say
“gi-normous” because it’s not a word.
Whoever plugged our tailpipe waited for us to
pass out and then put the body on the lawn.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 45.
CONTINUED:
TWO CORONER ATTENDANTS
Lift the FROZEN BODY of VICTIM #3 onto a rolling gurney, cover
it with a sheet...
NED (CONT’D)
Wasn’t Mrs. Newsome peeling potatoes yesterday?
Maybe we were wrong about her.
Maybe she has gone blood simple. Stickin’ her
victims all up in snowmen.
Ned points to the icy body as the attendants walk past with it.
Kevin would know.
Let’s ask him--
The attendants hit a bump as they pass Ned and Emerson, and the
gurney tips, spilling Kevin Vanden Eykel’s body to the pavement
where we hear a SHATTERING SOUND. The attendants look down at the
body, STILL UNDER THE SHEET. One PULLS BACK the sheet exposing
the legs and feet, which are in several frozen pieces now.
(”not pleasant to see”)
--or not.
(off Emerson’s look)
I’m not touching that.
(”moving on”)
And I’m fine with that. Let’s go talk to Mrs.
Newsome.
The meat wagon attendants sheepishly gather the frozen human
remains as Emerson and Ned walk toward the font door. Then, a
FRUSTRATED YELL (from Abner) from inside the house freezes
everyone in their tracks.

scenes.heading: INT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - SECONDS LATER

lines.text: Emerson and Ned follow the cops inside to find Mrs. Newsome with
her head in her hands. Behind her, Abner is repeatedly running
into the wall in his motorized wheelchair.
What happened?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 46.
CONTINUED:
The insurance company rejected Abner again.
Nice meeting everyone! Come the holidays, I’ll
be sucking puréed turkey through a straw while
my organs putrefy, but you enjoy yourselves.
Do you know who it was who called from the
insurance company?
Why? Do you want to send him a card, too?
Send who a card?
Mr. Kaiser. The Wish-a-Wish lady called. When
I told her about Abner, she said she wanted to
let Mr. Kaiser know about her foundation.
The Wish-a-Wish lady...
She’s a Killer-a-Killer!
And Kaiser’s a dead man if we don’t get to him
first.
OFF THEIR EXIT...
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY

lines.text: START ON THE MOSTLY-EATEN PIE, PULL OUT as Lily puts another
slice on her plate and eats while Olive and Vivian speak:
In Bulgaria, we were en route to a competition
and a band of gypsies stopped the train. They
came through the cabin and stole one woman’s
watch. And her soul.
They didn’t take her soul.
She was ornery and vacant after they left.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 47.
CONTINUED:
Because they took her watch.
I can’t imagine the adventures you’ve been on.
Perhaps those adventures were just the beginning.
Vivian notices half the pie is missing.
VIVIAN (CONT’D)
Oh, my. Lily, did you eat half a pie?
Lily stares into middle distance.
Are you feeling all right?
LILY’S POV - VIVIAN AND OLIVE
Looking back at her, curious and concerned. Something moves on
the coffee table. TILT DOWN:
A WEDGE OF CHEESE on the cheese plate is rocking back-and-forth.
Then, some hermit crab legs fold out and the cheese walks to the
edge of the table and scurries toward the hall.
ON LILY
She blinks, trying to understand what she just saw.
What did you put in that pie?
Just vanilla.
There wasn’t any vanilla in that pie.
As Olive wondered what exactly she did put in
Lily and Vivian’s pie...
OMIT
Closed, empty of customers.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 48.
CONTINUED:
...Chuck considered the risk she’d taken by
sharing her secret with the man from below
the ground.
Chuck rolls out dough on the table.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
She wondered what he would discover in the
swath of brunette truth she had given up.
The front doorbells JINGLE.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And then...
OSCAR (O.S.)
Hello, Chuck.
ANGLE - OSCAR
Stands right beside her. She startles.
You sneak up on people, which could get you
inadvertently bludgeoned with a rolling pin in
a place like this.
I find a bludgeoning to be an unique sensory
experience. I taste pennies and smell burnt
toast. I’m here to return the hair.
He holds up a small envelope, not yet handing it over.
My hair?
It’s a gesture. Of trust. I could treat it
like the dog’s hair. Test it. Reduce its
secrets to the numbers on a periodic chart.
Then why don’t you?
Because numbers won’t tell the whole story.
You know everything the hair has to tell. I’d
rather hear it from you.
She grabs the envelope. He doesn’t yet let go--
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 49.
CONTINUED: (2)
OSCAR (CONT’D)
And I think you want to tell me.
She smiles. He lets go and she takes the envelope.
OSCAR (CONT’D)
Well?
You should have asked the hair when you had
the chance.
Oscar reacts to the change of heart...
In that moment, Chuck realized her hate and
sadness had begun to thaw. There was only one
person with whom she wished to share the
burden of an impossible secret: the Pie-Maker.

scenes.heading: INT. NED’S CAR/PARKING STRUCTURE - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Driving up and around, one level at a time.
Who had just arrived at the Über-Life Life
Insurance parking structure with Emerson Cod,
in an attempt to find Steve Kaiser...

scenes.heading: INT. PARKING STRUCTURE - HIGHER FLOOR - SAME TIME

lines.text: Steve Kaiser tries to open his door, but it’s frozen shut.
...before and act of Kindness found him.
(frustrated)
What are the chances of that?
He fails to notice the WISH-A-WISH FOUNDATION VAN creeping to a
stop behind him. OFF STONE-COLD KILLER Madeline McLean...
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 50.
FADE IN:
Ned wheels around a corner, TIRES SQUEALING, as he and Emerson
head up the ramp.
As Emerson and Ned closed in on the killer
wish-maker...
Steve Kaiser still tries to get into his car. He’s crouched
down, using his BREATH to try to WARM THE DOORJAMB.
...the wish-maker had already found her next
snowman.
Stupid frozen door...
Behind him, Madeline slides out of the van, and stealthily
approaches, bat in hand. Steve gives the door a serious jerk.
It flies open, SLAMMING into the car next to it.
STEVE KAISER (CONT’D)
Ooh, shoot. A ding.
He turns back as she swings Kindness toward him, but he dives
out of the way. CRASH! The bat slams into the car door. As he
scrambles to avoid her next crack of the bat...
They continue driving up the ramps, through the structure...
Odds are we’re close. We’re almost at the top.
What are the odds of you having a daughter?
Because you’ve never actually mentioned it
before--
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 51.
CONTINUED:
First off, you’re like my grandfather and you
slow down when you talk, so you need to stop
talking. Second off, what I said to you
wasn’t said in the “We should talk more about
this later” way. It was said in the “I regret
saying this, there must be a potato in the
tailpipe” way. So stop talking.
I just didn’t want you to think--
(looking forward)
Stop.
I’ve been so focused on myself lately--
STOP THE CAR!
THEIR POV
Ned hits the breaks as they round the corner. The Wish-a-Wish
van is parked on the ramp, facing them, headlights on. Madeline
is between them and her van, SMASHING THE BAT down, nearly
missing Kaiser.
Ned and Emerson hop out. Emerson pulls a gun from his belt.
Madeline pauses as Kaiser cowers. A standoff:
EMERSON (CONT’D)
You need to stop wildin’ on the insurance
adjustor, ma’am.
What if I have a gun, too?
Madeline pulls an even bigger gun out of her pocket. Points it
at Emerson. Emerson drops his gun.
You don’t need to do this, Madeline. Please put
the gun and the bat down. Or definitely the gun.
Is that your wish?
I’m sorry?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 52.
CONTINUED: (2)
Because granting wishes is my job. And I’ll
grant yours and put this gun down. Right after
I knock one more thing off my wish list...
Still pointing the gun at Emerson with one hand... she gets
ready to swing at Kaiser with her free, bat-wielding hand.
As Madeline McLean prepared to grant one last
deadly desire...
POV - OUT THE FRONT WINDSHIELD AT the scene from behind
Madeline’s back. A SMALL MONKEY jumps up on the dash, looking
out at Madeline.
...Bobo, the bonobo monkey previously purchased
as a Wish-a-Wish gift for Abner Newsome...
PUSH IN ON THE MONKEY covetously eyeing the shifter.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...had a wish of its own. Its wish was to play
with the ball on a stick called “the shifter.”
The monkey jumps down onto the shifter, knocking it out of gear.
The van begins to roll.
Ned and Emerson await their fate -- hands in the air. CAMERA
PUSHES IN CLOSE ON Madeline as she cocks her weapon, her eyes
mad.
And so its wish was granted.
All of a sudden, the van rolls INTO FRAME behind the
unsuspecting Madeline. WHAM! With the monkey leaping about on
the dashboard, the van RUNS HER DOWN.
OMIT
The van has come to a rest against the parking structure wall.
As was the wish of Madeline McLean...
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 53.
CONTINUED:
As Emerson and Ned rush up to it, we REVEAL Madeline’s legs
sticking out from under the rear of the van.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...for though her sanity was torn asunder by a
boy named Abner Newsome...
And with that, CAMERA RISES UP OVER THE VAN and races over the
top of it to REVEAL Madeline’s head sticking out from under the
front bumper -- her body obviously (and tastefully) severed.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and her body was torn apart by a bonobo
named Bobo -- her heart was still intact, which
allowed her to grant one final wish.
CAMERA PUSHES IN on her smiling face -- even in death.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The facts were these: Madeline McLean had a
predilection for people pleasing.

scenes.heading: INT. CHILD’S BEDROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK (ONE WALL)

lines.text: PULL OUT from the white cast of a CHILD with a broken arm.
PULL BACK FURTHER TO REVEAL Madeline McLean is dressed as
Santa’s elf and dancing in front of the child.
She was a dream come true at the Wish-a-Wish
Foundation, where she provided succor with
suckers, coaxed chuckles from colics.
The child smiles. Madeline’s face beams with pride.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Madeline, perky, puts a GIFT BASKET on Abner’s bedside table.
He scowls.
But she met her match in Abner Newsome... the
little boy who lacked a heart.
Hi. I’m Maddy. Why don’t you tell me about
your super-special-self, sweetheart?
This basket smells like ass.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 54.
CONTINUED:
Madeline’s face falls...
OMIT
POP OF: MADELINE TAP-DANCING
In the traditional top hat and tails.
And though she tried and tried...
She finales with jazz hands, out of breath--
I said “lap dance,” not “tap dance”!
...she couldn’t make him happy.
There must be something you wish for.
I wish all those insurance company jerks who
keep rejecting me would drop dead.
Until she realized the boy without a heart
wanted revenge.
OFF MADELINE’S FACE: Something snaps. Her eyes fill with crazy.
BACK TO SCENE
Madeline lies motionless and severed under the van.
And in life, Madeline McLean had nearly made
that wish come true. But in death...
CLOSE ON the expression on Madeline’s dead (but not gory) face.
Glazed eyes. But something like a smile playing on her lips.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. ABNER NEWSOME’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY

lines.text: Abner sits propped up in his hospice bed, scowling at the world.
...she granted a far greater gift.
Emerson enters.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 55.
CONTINUED:
Heard you got a new heart?
It’s awesome. Now my bedsores are engorged.
Pretty amazing coincidence. That Madeline’s
heart would be a match. Almost like it was
meant to be.
Abner shrugs, looks away.
Emerson Cod thought of his own child and what
he would do if she were heartless in spite of
a new heart...
I brought you some cash.
(tosses a bag on the bed)
Two grand. The reward from the case. We
thought you and your mom should have it.
Despite himself, Abner smiles. Emerson clocks the smile--
This isn’t a smile. Probably just a tumor
pinching my facial nerve.
Emerson smiles...
While Emerson Cod bid a fond farewell to Abner
Newsome...
Ned walks through a cemetery. He sees a forlorn figure, seated
on the snow.
...the Pie-Maker came upon another heart in
need of repair...
He approaches, gingerly.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His own.
Chuck?
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 56.
CONTINUED:
Chuck looks up, takes him in, no longer needs to escape. She
brushes the snow off the grave--
There’s no headstone for me yet. We wait a
year.
(then)
How did you know I was here?
Because I have been everywhere else first.
He gets a little smile.
NED (CONT’D)
Is “a little while” over yet? Because I can’t
bear the thought of you hating me still.
I’m feeling better. And I had an idea.
She brushes some snow off of an adjacent tombstone. It reads:
“CHARLES CHARLES.” Ned catches on:
No.
I thought for one minute...
I’m not going to bring him back just so you
can watch me kill him again.
(resolved)
I can’t do that to you. I won’t.
Tears roll down Chuck’s cheek, but she doesn’t push the issue.
She knows he’s right about this.
Chuck wished things were different. She
wished she knew her father. She wished she
knew her mother. She wished the Pie-Maker
could comfort her by holding her close.
Ned kneels with her, carefully puts his coat around her
shoulders.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Not all those wishes were meant to be. But
one of them was...
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 57.
CLOSE ON Lily, speaking with someone OFF CAMERA.
I love the quiet on a snowy night.
A FEMALE VOICE responds in dulcet tones. It almost sounds like
air bubbles are escaping as she talks.
VOICE (O.S.)
Blurbur.
No, I feel fine. Much better now.
VOICE (O.S.)
Blubee blura?
Stop it. You’re the one who should be cold.
POP OUT WIDE TO REVEAL Lily is talking to a MERMAID that’s
floating in the air before her.
Bru bllur blur.
It was good pie.
(then)
When Charlotte was young, after we’d moved in,
she used to stand, right there where you’re
floating -- and watch the snow with me.
Blur bur bur.
At night, while she slept, I would sneak into
the backyard and make two snow angels. She
never said anything and I’d always play dumb.
She thought they were her parents.
Blurp?
One was her father... the other one was me.
REVEAL OLIVE is standing where the mermaid is, having this
conversation with a still-tripping Lily.
PUSHING DAISIES #108 "Corpsicle" 11/04/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 58.
CONTINUED:
You?
I’m Chuck’s mother.
ANGLE - OLIVE: As she recovers from this revelation.
OMIT
